system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    40% SMB discount: signup +31%, rev +18%, monthly retain -12pp; segment def unchanged.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to match with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that carries hard numbers and they are unfavorable for the stated objective: +31% signup and +18% revenue bought at -12pp monthly retention, with the segment definition unchanged so the retention drop is not a mix artifact. Discounting into a price war would inflate short-run signups while degrading the durable revenue base, which is exactly the opposite of the primary objective. Referral incentives (memory_57) were validated in established customers and do not address the two metrics that are actually deteriorating. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but orthogonal to an SMB-side funnel decline.

That leaves the two funnel levers. Onboarding completion (-4%) sits upstream of activation (-6%), so a fix at the onboarding stage plausibly propagates into activation, whereas activation messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom in accounts that may never have finished onboarding. I therefore intend simplify_onboarding.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than diversifying across levers, because these two are the entire evidentiary basis for my chosen action and they look suspiciously like they may be the same underlying experiment consolidated twice at different dates (day 52 and day 12), one described as "shortening onboarding" and one as "cutting required fields at signup." If so, my apparent two-source support collapses to one source, and the effect size is smaller than the memory set implies. Both are also compressed to directional claims with no magnitudes, no durations, and no retention or revenue-quality readouts, unlike memory_73 which retained its numbers. Pulling the originals tells me whether the lift was durable, how large it was, and on which cohort.

Downstream value risk: memory_31's mechanism is removing required signup fields. Those fields are frequently what qualifies and routes a lead. Removing them can raise activation counts while lowering the share of accounts that are genuinely qualified, so the metric improves while sustainable qualified revenue does not. This is the same shape of trap as memory_73 — a headline gain concealing a quality loss — and the compressed memory would not have recorded it. I am running at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, with retention and downstream lead-quality/qualified-pipeline instrumented as guardrails alongside completion rate, not completion rate alone. If verification shows the two memories are one experiment or that qualification data was never tracked, I will narrow to a guarded test and reconsider activation_messaging, which carries less lead-quality exposure.
